answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with sponsored apprenticeship. A new identity starts with no standing and earns it by completing a chain of jobs for established members, each job unlocking larger privileges on the climb toward the summit of full standing. A sponsor acts as the velvet rope, staking standing on each apprentice, and a prism of the apprentice's job history travels with every deal, so misbehavior docks the sponsor too. Forging a thousand identities means a thousand chains and a thousand sponsors risking standing, and that history cannot be bought in bulk.
